about: The one table behind Speed up (quantization/speed_up.py reads it): one row per engine. The core is engine-neutral; a row names the module in quantization/head_writers/ that holds that engine's parts, and the names of its functions: stock (is this engine stock), plan (the output layer and whether the target is lighter), write (the copy), accuracy (original against copy), and optionally speed (decode rows at given contexts and batches) with device (target id, name, backend, memory_bytes and budget_bytes the engine may use of the GPU in this machine; speed results are a list in the copy's record, one entry per GPU); a row without speed is kept on accuracy alone. formats are checkpoint formats (head_writers.detect), never model names. runs says whether the engine is built; why says why not. Adding an engine is a row and a writer module, no core edit. parts maps each part (the parts table below) the engine writes to its plan function and what its writer needs (file: the new weights' file, whose presence also marks a source that already has the part light; targets; prefix: where the part's modules sit in this engine's checkpoints); mtp names the function that measures speed with MTP on (mtp_ks: the one that says the draft counts it starts from), returning per depth the context, each prompt's tok/s without drafts (base) and at each k (ks), and each prompt's output hash (tokens). One part per run: a part added to a copy is a copy of that copy, gated against it, with the links into it hashed in the record.

parts.label: output layer
parts.about: lm_head: read on every token, so it changes the main model's answers: the next-token agreement gate, then plain decode speed. untied: refused when config.json ties it to the embedding

parts.label: MTP draft layer
parts.note: not checked: only the MTP draft layer changed and every drafted token is checked by the main model; outputs can still differ at floating-point near-ties, as they do with MTP itself (the record counts the prompts whose tokens match between the arms)
parts.about: the draft layer's Linear modules the checkpoint keeps unquantized (the engine row's prefix and the checkpoint's ignore list). Every drafted token is checked by the main model, so outputs differ only at floating-point near-ties, as with MTP itself and with any recompiled graph (2026-11-12: k=3 against k=0 on one copy matched 1 of 8 short prompts; a byte-identical main model in a new compiled graph matched 2 of 8 short and 7 of 8 long): no agreement gate, the matching prompts recorded, not gated (note). The gate is speed with MTP on, run source, copy, source again on the same prompts (at least min_prompts) and the same long-depth real text (data/mtp_long_corpus.json; the arms' input ids are compared by hash), each without drafts and at each draft count k: the source and the copy each run the derived sweep (core/draft_count.sweep_next: from collectors/mtp.KS, one k more while a larger one could still win), and the source runs again at every k either sweep reached. Per prompt, the copy at its best k over the source at its best k (the source's two runs averaged where both ran that k, else its second run; each arm's best k by median tok/s, chosen again inside every bootstrap resample of the prompts, seed 0); kept only if the lower end of the 95% interval of the median is above 1 plus the source's own change between its two runs (at the source's best k, or the largest change over the ks both its runs share when its first sweep stopped short of that k), at every depth. Recorded beside it: the factor with MTP over without (each arm over its own run without drafts; each arm compiles its own graph) and the factor without drafts (copy over source), whose product is the headline. The baseline is the source: the original, or the copy this part is added to (a second command: derive one part per run)

threshold.about: the copy must give the original's most likely next token at least this share of the time (point estimate) pooled over the documents of data/gate_corpus.json (8 Project Gutenberg excerpts of natural prose the original did not write, hashed here; a different hash refuses). Set by the owner 2026-11-10 after the review found the original's own continuation too easy a text; the threshold did not move. The interval is clustered by document. Fewer scored positions than min_positions and the gate refuses to decide

expect.about: Seconds each stage is expected to take: floor + per_gib x the checkpoint's GiB. NOT MEASURED: set by hand 2026-11-10 from the order of magnitude of the first runs, so a screen shows them as an estimate (about) until a run's own step times replace them.

mtp.about: The MTP part's speed_measure, derived from what quantization/speed_up.measure_mtp runs (mtp_seconds): engine starts (each run's k=0 and one per k, from the row's mtp_ks to core/draft_count.K_MAX) x per_start (the long depth is the shipped real text, data/mtp_long_corpus.json, nothing generated first since 2026-11-12: the term for the source's own continuation, 5.4 s per GiB per 1k tokens, is gone). MEASURED on one run only (one point: 27B, RTX 5090, vLLM 0.31), 2026-11-12, a 27B compressed-tensors copy of 16.45 GiB (storage/boltbeam-runs/derive-mtp-27b-20261112, log times in the copy's speed_up_mtp): 134 to 150 s per start in the source and copy runs, median 139; the source's first k=0 took 854 s, 715 s more than a start. That run swept the source and the copy to the K_MAX cap, so it sits at the TOP of the range: its measurement took 5,093 s (84.9 min; source 2,235, copy 1,600, source again 1,258 at 114 s a start) against 5,302 s (88.4 min) estimated; the job (write and the three runs) 85.2 min, 5,109 s, each run sweeping k=1..10 (all hit the then K_MAX cap of 10 at the long depth; that depth was the model's own looping continuation, so those sweeps followed repetition, not text; the top of the range, k=16, is extrapolated by the formula, unmeasured). The low end (each sweep stopping at its first ks) has never been measured, so it is likely optimistic. The split of per_start into floor and per GiB is set by hand (one size measured)
